sections.h2: Whom to call about a Glynn County tax bill
sections.html:
The job is divided between two offices. The Tax Commissioner sends bills and takes payments at 1725 Reynolds Street, Suite 100, Brunswick, phone 912-554-7000, and its counter keeps weekday hours of 8:00 to 4:30. The Property Appraisal Office, Suite 101 in the same building at 912-554-7093, sets values and answers exemption and appeal questions from 8:30 to 5:00 each weekday.

The tax commissioner's page lists the office's duties as billing, collecting and distributing ad valorem and title ad valorem taxes, holding delinquent tax sales and preparing the yearly digest. If you are selling, call the tax side for balances, liens and split bills, and the appraisal side for anything about value or a missing exemption.

Glynn County covers the southeast Georgia coast, with Brunswick as the county seat. Its Sea Islands include Jekyll Island, St. Simons Island and Sea Island. The county has 87,599 residents, up 3.7 percent from the 2020 census count, and 45,747 housing units. Owners occupy 66.7 percent of homes, and the median owner-occupied home is worth $301,300. Median household income is $69,799, and builders pulled 448 permits during 2025.

Brunswick is the one incorporated city. A house on St. Simons or on a mainland road outside the city is therefore taxed through the county. Ask the tax commissioner whether your parcel carries any extra district charge.

sections.h2: When Glynn County bills go out and come due
sections.html:
Glynn sends one yearly bill covering land, buildings and business personal property. The 2026 bills were mailed September 17, appeared online September 18, and are due November 17, 2026. The schedule can shift depending on when the state accepts the digest.

Glynn County tax year, from January valuation to the autumn bill
WhenWhat happens
January 1Use and condition of a property fix its value for that tax year
April 1Last day for homestead exemption, returns and preferential assessment requests
May and JuneAnnual assessment notices go out
June and JulyAppeal window of 45 days, with the exact date on each notice
September 1Digest is submitted to the Georgia Department of Revenue
September and OctoberTax bills are mailed
Mobile homesMailed in January, always due April 1

Waiting costs interest first. It starts the day after the due date, is figured monthly, and follows a rate set at the federal level. On top of that sits a 5 percent charge on the unpaid principal for each 120 day period, topping out at 20 percent of the bill. Levy fees begin only after the collection process starts.

  • The tax commissioner sends a written notice after the payment deadline passes.
  • Thirty days later, with no payment, a Fi.Fa. (execution) is issued against the owner and the parcel. The issuance fee is $13.00.
  • The execution is then recorded on the general execution docket kept by the superior court clerk.
  • Money received is applied to the oldest year owed, and partial payments are possible only through the online portal.

If you are behind and plan to list, request a payoff figure first. An execution on record has to be satisfied before a buyer can take clean title.

File the homestead application by April 1. You can apply at any point after the house becomes your primary residence, through April 1 of the year you first want the benefit, and a missed application is treated as a waiver. The appraisal office can tell you which local exemptions fit your address and which papers it wants to see.

A challenge to value starts with your annual assessment notice. The appeal must be postmarked within 45 days of the notice's mailing and sent to the assessors' board. Glynn's calendar puts that stretch in June and July. Separately, a claim for tax that was assessed or collected in error has to be started within three years after the payment.

A short list of calls and documents keeps the sale on track. Ask the Tax Commissioner at 912-554-7000 whether your bill for the year has been issued and paid, and whether any older year or execution sits on the parcel. Ask the Property Appraisal Office at 912-554-7093 to confirm which exemptions are on file and whether an appeal is still open.

Gather the assessment notice, your latest bill and any payment receipt. Buyers on the coast often ask about carrying costs, so having the actual bill ready answers that quickly. If you hold a mobile home, remember its bill is mailed in January and always due April 1, separate from the land.

The office takes payments online, by mail, at the counter and in drop boxes at the front and back of the Harold Pate building. An online card payment adds a service fee of 2.95 percent, never less than $2.50, and an electronic check adds $1.50. Those fees go to the payment vendor and card companies, since the office keeps none of them. Mail checks to Glynn County Tax Commissioner, 1725 Reynolds Street, Suite 100, Brunswick, GA 31520.

Write these on or enclose them with a mailed payment:

  • The parcel number or bill number.
  • The property address.
  • A current phone number.
  • The payment coupon or a copy of the bill, and a stamped return envelope if you want a receipt.

The bill follows the January 1 owner. A separate bill goes to a new owner around the same time or late in the year, and the obligation stays with whoever owns the parcel at that point. Who reimburses whom comes from the contract. Lenders do not get copies, so a borrower with an escrow account should ask the servicer to confirm it received the bill.

sections.h2: Who settles the tax bill when a house sells?
sections.html:
Whoever runs the closing requests the open balance from the tax commissioner, and unpaid tax is deducted from what the seller receives. Because the bill is built on the January 1 owner, a sale partway through the year normally needs a proration written into the contract. Ask whether the bill for your sale year has been issued yet, and keep the receipt from any payment so the closing agent can match it to the parcel.

We buy Glynn County houses as-is, including mainland lots with a delinquent balance or a recorded execution. A cash purchase still runs through a title search, and the tax payoff is cleared in the same way. If you inherited a coastal house that needs repairs, send us the parcel number. For a property passing under a recorded beneficiary deed, our Georgia transfer on death page explains the steps.

faqs.q: What is the 2026 due date for Glynn County property tax?
faqs.a: November 17, 2026. The county mailed bills on September 17 and posted them online on September 18, 2026.

faqs.q: When must a Glynn County assessment appeal be filed?
faqs.a: Count 45 days from the mailing date shown on your assessment notice. Notices go out in May and June, so the window falls in June and July.

faqs.q: Will the lender on my Glynn County home receive the tax bill?
faqs.a: No. The tax commissioner does not send bills directly to mortgage companies. A borrower who pays through escrow should confirm with the servicer that the bill arrived.

faqs.q: Are installment payments allowed on Glynn County property tax?
faqs.a: Only partial payments, and only online. Georgia does not allow increment payments on current year taxes before the digest is accepted and a bill exists.

faqs.q: What does a late Glynn County tax payment cost?
faqs.a: Monthly interest plus a 5 percent penalty on the past due principal every 120 days, capped at 20 percent. Levy fees are added once that process begins.
